name: Treaty with the Sauk, 1815 (Sauk of the Missouri River, Portage des Sioux)
aka: Treaty of peace and friendship with the Sac of the Missouri River, September 13, 1815
nations: Sauk (Thakiwaki) then living on the Missouri River
promises: The Sauk of the Missouri River assented to the treaty of St. Louis of November 3, 1804 with the united Sauk and Fox and promised to help re-establish it (Article 1).
They promised to remain separate from the Sauk of Rock River until peace was made with them (Article 2).
The United States promised them all rights secured by the 1804 treaty and, as soon as practicable, a just proportion of its annuities, while they complied (Article 3).
compensation: No land was ceded by this treaty; it promised a share of the 1804 annuities.
today: The Sac and Fox claim for the lands ceded in 1804 was heard in Indian Claims Commission Docket 83 (interlocutory order of June 12, 1959 on title). That claim concerns the 1804 treaty and is not recorded as a breach of this 1815 treaty.

nationVoice.nation: Sac and Fox Nation of Missouri in Kansas and Nebraska
nationVoice.summary: The Nation says the Treaty of 1815 officially named the Sac and Fox of Missouri a distinct tribe and moved the band from Iowa and Illinois to northeast Missouri, after the 1804 treaty, which Black Hawk did not accept as valid, had ceded Saukenuk, and before the Treaty of 1837 moved the band across the Missouri River into Kansas.
